Topic 1: Measurement and Dimensions of P.competency: Uses a variety of instruments to accurately measure physical quantities and applies the concept of dimensions to establish relations between quantities.
outcomes: a) Measure a variety of physical quantities with minimal errors
b) Analyse dimensions of derived quantities and use them to check consistency of equations

Topic 2: Statics.competency: Investigates the effect of forces on a system and how centre of gravity relates to the stability of mechanical structures.
outcomes: a) Determine the resultant of vectors in different situations
b) Appreciate concepts of moments and torque in construction of structures

Topic 1: Introduction to Economics.competency: The learner analyses fundamental economic concepts and principles to make informed decisions about the use of scarce resources for personal and national development.
outcomes: a) Analyse the basic economic problem of scarcity, choice and opportunity cost in real-life situations
b) Evaluate different economic systems and their implications for resource allocation
c) Apply the concept of the production possibility frontier to real-life trade-off decisions
d) Analyse economic data and statistics using appropriate tools to inform decisions

Topic 2: Price Theory.competency: The learner analyses market behaviour and price determination mechanisms to evaluate how individuals, businesses and governments make resource allocation decisions.
outcomes: a) Analyse the theory of demand and factors that influence demand in real markets
b) Analyse the theory of supply and factors that influence supply in real markets
c) Apply the concept of market equilibrium to explain price determination
d) Evaluate elasticity of demand and supply and their implications for business and government policy
e) Assess price mechanism and price control policies and their effects on markets
f) Analyse causes and effects of price fluctuations in commodity markets

Topic 3: Production and Market Structure.competency: The learner evaluates production processes and market structures to assess how firms make decisions about output, pricing and competition in real-world contexts.
outcomes: a) Analyse factors of production and their role in determining output and costs
b) Evaluate different market structures (perfect competition, monopoly, oligopoly, monopolistic competition) and their implications for consumers and producers
c) Assess pricing strategies used by firms under different market conditions

Topic 1: Introduction to ICT.competency: The learner operates a variety of ICTs to perform tasks in day-to-day life.
outcomes: a) Identify and explain how ICT tools are used in different fields of life
b) Operate basic ICT devices safely and responsibly in everyday contexts
c) Appreciate the social, ethical and legal issues related to ICT use
